cards.anchor: Reach the stipulated bounded uniformity proxy: three elevation-vial attenuations with normalized spread at most 4 percent when sampling begins at second 120, reducing stirring time if feasible. One observed 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and returned 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This supports one bounded counterexample to universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm; repeated success remains a hypothesis.
cards.burden: Use at most six fresh trials in the 90-minute session, with manual five-second image checks, reference readings and three depth samples per trial. Existing available resources suffice. The schedule uses 60 commanded stirring seconds per trial; savings against the preferred procedure cannot be claimed without its actual stopping times. Limited replication and manual handling constrain confidence.
cards.construction: Hypothesis: a fixed 300 rpm, 60-second bulk rotation can repeatedly achieve the final-vial proxy without stable side images. For each trial, rinse the vessel and prepare 150 mL tap water plus 0.30 mL dye in the 250 mL beaker. Use one dye bottle, fixed addition location, locked camera settings and common block references. Command 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, then stop regardless of side spread. Do not stir again or restart before sampling at second 120. Record side images every five seconds without allowing them to control operation. Withdraw 1 mL at each marked 10, 28 and 45 mm depth within ten seconds after second 120, alternating bottom-first and top-first order. Calculate attenuation against the water reference and spread as maximum minus minimum divided by mean. Keep the spill tray in use and stop if liquid escapes.
cards.defeat: Precommit that every completed repeat must meet the at-most-4-percent final-vial criterion to support repeatable success in this session. Any target failure defeats that session-level all-pass prediction; repeated failures or a systematic relationship with sampling order strengthen the rival. Reference or recipe failures make the affected comparison uninterpretable. None of these outcomes establishes that 900 rpm or optical stability is necessary.
cards.mutation: Replace optical-gated continuation at 900 rpm with a precommitted lower-speed duration. Preserve the independent final-vial target and keep optical readings as observations only.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis prediction: repeated final-vial spreads are at most 4 percent after 60 seconds of commanded stirring, including trials whose side checks fail the optical threshold. Repeated success would support dispensability of the preferred dependency for this recipe and protocol, without identifying the cause of optical fluctuations.
cards.prediction_rival: Rival prediction: repeated final-vial spreads exceed 4 percent, or results depend systematically on sampling order, despite the earlier successful trial. Either pattern undermines repeatable success of this fixed intervention; order dependence particularly supports sampling-mediated readings.
cards.probe: Run up to six fixed 300 rpm, 60-second repeats, alternating sampling order while holding recipe, dye addition and camera conditions fixed. Log commanded speed, cessation time, five-second side-region readings, every syringe withdrawal, reference repeatability, raw final-vial readings, normalized spread and every target failure. Compare final target attainment across repeats and sampling orders; never rescue a failure with additional stirring. Stable side images alone do not count as success.
cards.rival: Hypothesis: the stipulated successful trial was exceptional or its sampling disturbed remaining gradients; fixed lower-speed stirring does not reliably deliver the final proxy.
unknowns: Only one successful fixed lower-speed trial is observed; repeatability and causal sufficiency are unresolved.
Matched final-vial results and total duration for the preferred 900 rpm procedure are absent, preventing comparative uniformity or time-saving claims.
Sampling can disturb gradients; alternating order exposes some order effects but cannot eliminate all sampling bias.
Common-aliquot repeatability is not concentration calibration; nominal rpm has no independent verification.
Speck identity and causal contribution remain unverified. This probe cannot establish bubbles or explain the 900 rpm image fluctuations.
Other viscosities, solutes, vessel sizes and continuous processes remain untested; the synthetic proxy establishes no real chemical or human benefit.
